# CivicPlus - AI Enablement Engineer (Product & Product Operations)

## Job Details
- **Company:** CivicPlus
- **Role:** AI Enablement Engineer (Product & Product Operations)
- **Location:** Remote, United States
- **Type:** Full time
- **Salary Range:** $119,100 – $181,100
- **Target Ask:** $140,000 – $160,000
- **URL:** https://civicpluscareers.ttcportals.com/jobs/17740995-ai-enablement-engineer-product-and-product-operations
- **Cover letter:** Required

## Key Requirements
- 5-8 years in software engineering, automation engineering, data engineering, ML engineering, solutions engineering, or similar
- Experience building/supporting AI-enabled workflows, automations, internal tools, system integrations
- Proficiency in Python or JavaScript
- APIs, integration patterns, structured/unstructured data
- LLM concepts: prompt design, evaluation, model/service integration
- Cloud platforms and developer tooling
- Strong written/verbal communication, explaining technical to non-technical
- Documenting workflows, standards, technical solutions
- Comfort with sensitive/regulated data

## Preferred
- Workflow automation platforms, data pipelines, governance controls, experimentation, internal enablement/change management
- Responsible AI practices, model evaluation, AI operations
- Product operations, product analytics, product strategy with strong technical skills
- GovRAMP, FedRAMP, or similar frameworks
- AI-first product workflows (not just adding AI features)

## Role Summary
Design, build, and maintain AI-enabled tools, workflows, and internal automations.
Partner with cross-functional teams to identify high-value AI use cases.
Translate business problems into scalable technical solutions (prompts, orchestration, data pipelines).
Establish best practices for responsible AI: security, privacy, testing, monitoring, documentation.
Provide technical guidance, training, and enablement to internal teams.
Operate within GovRAMP-relevant, security-conscious environments.
Bridge product strategy to AI delivery.

## Match Assessment
- STRONG: Building AI workflows and automations (CoSH, FlareGuard)
- STRONG: Cross-functional collaboration (product/engineering/marketing/support)
- STRONG: Translating business problems into AI solutions
- STRONG: Responsible AI governance, output validation, quality enforcement
- STRONG: Evaluating AI tools and models (Claude, Gemini, GPT via OpenRouter)
- STRONG: Documentation, technical standards, reusable patterns
- STRONG: Training and enablement (FlareGuard built for team adoption)
- STRONG: Communication — explaining complex AI to non-technical audiences
- MODERATE: JavaScript/TypeScript (Python adjacent)
- MODERATE: APIs, integration patterns
- MODERATE: Cloud platforms, deployment
- WEAK: 5-8 years software engineering title (7 years tech writing + AI engineering)
- WEAK: GovRAMP/FedRAMP experience
- WEAK: Product operations/analytics background

fit.reasoning: Strong overlap in AI workflow enablement, prompt design, technical documentation, and remote/salary fit; the main gap is deeper software/automation engineering and cloud/data/regulated-environment experience, but the candidate's 3 years as an AI Workflow Engineer partially offsets that.
red_flags: Primary experience is technical writing; only 3 of 7 years are AI workflow engineering, so the 5–8 year software/automation engineering requirement is not a clean match.
Python is intermediate only, with no clear cloud platform, API/data pipeline, or sensitive/regulated data experience.
Several preferred areas like Responsible AI practices, model evaluation, product analytics, and GovRAMP/FedRAMP are not reflected in the profile.

resume_bullets: Designed and deployed FlareGuard, an AI-enabled content validation workflow, reducing support escalations by 70–80% through automated document QA and gap detection.
Partnered with Support and Engineering to identify high-value AI use cases, translating business needs into automated prompt workflows and system integrations.
Migrated 500+ Zendesk articles with conditional content and AI-assisted categorization, ensuring accurate, role-based delivery for in-app help systems.
Redesigned 200-article help portal with role-aware navigation and AI-driven search enhancements, improving self-service deflection for thousands of daily users.
Built a Python-based PDF generation pipeline integrated with existing systems, resolving a years-long customer complaint and enabling on-demand documentation delivery.
Established documentation standards and AI workflow best practices, providing technical training to cross-functional teams to enable scalable adoption.
materials.cover_letter:
Your AI Enablement Engineer role sits at the intersection of building tools and making people capable of using them. That is exactly where my work has been for the past seven years. I do not hand off a workflow and walk away. I build it, document it, and train the people who depend on it.

At Redwood, I built FlareGuard, an AI content validation workflow that cut escalations by 70 to 80 percent. I redesigned a 200-article help portal with role-aware navigation, and I built a PDF pipeline that resolved a customer complaint open for years. At Bird, I migrated over 500 Zendesk articles with conditional content and built the release notes pipeline. Each project meant documenting the standards alongside the build, so the systems could be maintained and trusted.

You need someone who can design AI-enabled workflows, write the standards around them, and make sure internal teams actually use them. That is what I do. I would welcome the conversation.

short_answers.Why this company?: I'm drawn to CivicPlus because it sits at the intersection of AI and civic impact. I've spent my career building AI-enabled workflows that make complex information accessible—first for customer support, now for government operations. The opportunity to help local governments streamline communications and service delivery through practical AI tools aligns perfectly with my skills and my desire to make a tangible difference in people's lives.
short_answers.Tell us about yourself: Over the past five-plus years, I've evolved from technical writer to AI workflow engineer. At Redwood, I built FlareGuard, an AI-powered content validation system that cut escalations by 70-80%, and led the migration of 500+ articles into a role-aware help portal. I specialize in turning messy business problems into scalable AI solutions—designing prompts, integrating APIs, and partnering closely with engineering and support teams. I'm excited to bring that same human-centered, automation-first approach to CivicPlus, where I can help build internal tools and enablement practices that make AI adoption safe and effective.
